questions.prompt: A daimyo answered directly to the emperor, not the shogun

block.label: Swipe Sort
block.sub: Flick each card up into its bucket

questions.why: False — daimyo swore loyalty to the shogun, who held real power; the emperor was only a ceremonial figurehead with no command over them.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Act 1 Scene 1, who does Benvolio try to stop fighting?
questions.why: Benvolio draws his sword trying to break up the brawling servants, not to join the fight — Tybalt then arrives and accuses him of wanting war, not peace.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In C-Am-F-G, which chord sits between Am and G in the sequence?
questions.why: The progression runs C then Am then F then G, so F is the third chord, sitting right between Am and G.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.prompt: What did students mainly aim to capture in Paint Like a Beast?
questions.why: The goal was capturing the texture and movement of the animals through bold brushwork, not achieving photo-realistic likeness.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these groups in Japan's feudal system by how much land they typically controlled
questions.why: The shogun controlled the most territory overall, daimyo governed large regional domains granted to them, samurai held no land of their own but served those who did, and peasants farmed land owned by others.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these stages of a continuity-and-change enquiry by scale
questions.why: A continuity-and-change enquiry zooms outward: starting from one small detail, widening to an event, then a whole period, then the broadest era, to see what really shifted over time.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What do the Montagues and Capulets share, according to the Prologue?
questions.why: The Prologue describes the two households sharing 'an ancient grudge', establishing the feud that drives the whole tragedy.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What is the approximate span of years in which Shakespeare's plays were written?
questions.why: Shakespeare's plays were written roughly between 1590 and 1613, during the late Elizabethan and early Jacobean eras — well before 1650 and long after 1500.
